blocks.value: **Confusing the class with the object.** `Student` is the blueprint; `ana` is a student. You can have one class and a thousand objects.
**Thinking objects share data.** Each object has its own copy of the attributes. Changing one does not change another.

**Expecting `extends` and `implements` to be interchangeable.** `extends` inherits real behavior from one class. `implements` promises to supply behavior listed by an interface, and a class may implement several.

**Assuming OOP is always the right answer.** A twenty-line program that reads two numbers and adds them does not need a class. Objects earn their keep when a program has many parts that each own some state.
